questions.title: Bubble Sort
questions.summary: Compare adjacent values and steadily grow a sorted suffix.

approach.explanation: Walk adjacent pairs from left to right. A swap moves the largest remaining value to the end of the unsorted range; stop early when a pass makes no swaps.

questions.title: Two Sum
questions.inputHint: JSON object: { numbers: number[], target: number }

approach.explanation: Scan once, store each value with its index, and ask whether the current complement has already appeared.

visualBlueprint.representation: Array scan with a live complement hash-map inspection card.

questions.title: Binary Search
questions.summary: Halve a sorted search space using left, middle, and right bounds.
questions.inputHint: JSON object: { array: number[], target: number }

approach.explanation: Because the data is ordered, compare the middle value and discard half of the candidates on every iteration.

questions.title: Valid Palindrome
questions.summary: Move two pointers inward while skipping punctuation and case.
questions.defaultInput: {"text":"A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"}

approach.explanation: Ignore punctuation and case, then compare the outside pair. A mismatch settles the answer; a match allows both pointers to move inward.

questions.title: Longest Substring
questions.summary: Expand a unique-character window and move its left edge on duplicates.

approach.explanation: Record the last index of each character. When a duplicate lands in the active window, advance left past its earlier position without moving right backward.

questions.title: Reverse Linked List
questions.summary: Flip one next pointer per iteration without losing the remaining chain.
questions.inputHint: JSON array of integer node values

approach.explanation: Keep the unprocessed chain safe in nextTemp, then redirect curr.next toward prev before advancing both pointers.

questions.title: Inorder Traversal
questions.summary: Visit left, node, right with call stack context.

approach.explanation: An inorder traversal visits every left subtree, then its node, then the right subtree.

visualBlueprint.representation: Hierarchical binary tree with active node, traversal order, and call-stack panel.

questions.title: BFS / DFS
questions.summary: Compare breadth-first queue traversal with depth-first stack traversal on the same binary tree.
questions.inputHint: JSON object: { tree: level-order values (null for missing nodes), strategy: "BFS" | "DFS" }

approach.explanation: BFS visits a whole level at a time using a FIFO queue. DFS follows a branch using a LIFO stack (preorder here), pushing right before left so the left child is visited first.

questions.title: Number of Islands

approach.explanation: Each unvisited land cell starts a flood fill that marks one entire island before the scan continues.

visualBlueprint.representation: 2D land/water grid with visited cells, flood-fill frontier, and island count.

questions.title: Climbing Stairs

approach.explanation: The number of ways to reach each step is the sum of the previous two counts, so only two rolling values are needed.

visualBlueprint.representation: One-dimensional recurrence table plus optional recursion-tree view.

questions.title: Search Insert Position
questions.summary: Find the target index or the insertion position that preserves sorted order.
questions.inputHint: JSON object: { array: sorted number[], target: number }

approach.explanation: Perform binary search on the sorted array. If the target is found, return its index. If not found, when the search interval collapses (left > right), the left pointer points to the insertion index that maintains sorted order.

questions.title: Insert Into a Binary Search Tree
questions.summary: Follow the BST search path, insert element e, and observe the resulting tree height h.
questions.inputHint: JSON object: { tree: level-order BST, e: integer to insert }

approach.explanation: Compare e with each node and follow left for smaller values or right for larger values until an empty child is found. Duplicate values are ignored. Height h is the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path; an empty tree has height 0.

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.summary: Check that every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket in the correct order.
questions.inputHint: JSON object: { text: string made only of ( ) [ ] { } }

approach.explanation: Brackets must close in the reverse order they opened, which is exactly how a stack behaves (last in, first out). Push every opening bracket. When a closing bracket appears, the most recent unmatched opening bracket must be on top of the stack and must be the same type; otherwise the string is invalid. After the last character the stack must be empty, or some opening bracket was never closed.
